sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Retail of Desktop 3D Printers and Resin Filaments

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Belgo-Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU) Bilateral Investment Treaties in force
Luxembourg network of Double Taxation Agreements (90+ DTAAs, including LU-US, LU-CN, LU-UK)
Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU) and EU single-market freedoms
EU trade agreements applicable to online retail, including EU-Singapore Free Trade Agreement

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Loi modifiée du 12 novembre 2004 relative à la lutte contre le blanchiment et le financement du terrorisme; Loi du 13 janvier 2019 portant création d'un registre des bénéficiaires effectifs; Loi du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales, as amended by Loi du 10 juin 2015 introducing the SCSp; CSSF Regulation 12-02 and related Luxembourg AML/CFT implementing rules.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy and Apostille of passport of each ultimate beneficial owner and any limited partner holding 25% or more of the SCSp
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent notary or passport-issuing authority in the UBO's jurisdiction of nationality

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent company register extract for the corporate general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry of the general partner's jurisdiction of incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Duly notarized and apostilled power of attorney for the authorized Luxembourg representative or filing agent
Bank reference letter and source-of-funds confirmation for each partner/UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Financial institution maintaining the partner's or UBO's account

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence for politically exposed persons, their family members and close associates; screening of all partners, general partner, signatories and UBOs against the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, UN Security Council sanctions lists, OFAC SDN list, and Luxembourg Minister of Finance/FIU restrictive measures; documented source of wealth and source of funds; retention of AML/CFT records for at least five years after the termination of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Electronic Trade and Companies Register portal (RCSL eRegistres)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names may be submitted using Latin-alphabet characters; non-Latin script must be transliterated into Latin characters. Luxembourg statutory practice does not impose mandatory French or German translation for an SCSp, but the name must be distinguishable, lawful and not misleading. An English-only commercial name is acceptable for online retail of 3D printers and resin filaments.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Société / SA / SARL if not the actual legal form
SCSp / Société en commandite spéciale may be used only as the mandatory or voluntary legal-form suffix
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection by the LBR/RCSL, the applicant may file a reasoned administrative appeal with the Minister of Justice within 15 days of notification. Alternatively, a substantially distinct new name may be reserved immediately. The initial name reservation is renewable once for an additional 60 days before the submission of the incorporation filing.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible with conditions: a Luxembourg domiciliation provider may supply the registered office, but the SCSp must maintain genuine administrative substance in Luxembourg, including a local registered agent, accounting records, and AML/CFT files. A pure letterbox arrangement without local decision-making or records is not acceptable for regulated banking onboarding.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (approximately 5% annualized risk for a low-risk online retail SCSp; unannounced on-site inspections are uncommon but may occur during AML/CFT audits by the FIU, CSSF or RBE authorities).

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR/RCSL) name reservation fee
RCSL trade register filing and RESA (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations) publication for SCSp formation
Notarization, apostille and legalization of foreign UBO and corporate general partner documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary and issuing registry in origin jurisdiction
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing notarial and apostille fees in country of issuance

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: One-year registered office domiciliation service for the SCSp in Luxembourg City
Drafting and legal review of the SCSp limited partnership agreement (LPA) including UBO identification, AML/CFT clauses and e-commerce commercial scope
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing Luxembourg professional services market benchmark

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation AML compliance package: PEP and sanctions screening, UBO/RBE pre-filing review, and local registered agent onboarding
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg AML compliance provider / law firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing Luxembourg AML compliance market benchmark

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, in particular Articles 101 et seq. concerning the Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp), as amended by the Law of 23 July 2016.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), administered by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Signed partnership agreement (contrat de société) and the supporting registration declaration filed electronically through the Luxembourg Business Registers eDesk.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is prescribed for an SCSp and no escrow account is required. Capital is freely determined in the partnership agreement; in-kind contributions must be supported by a statutory auditor valuation report to the extent required by the Law of 10 August 1915.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The sole general partner of [Name] SCSp, acting as the management body, hereby resolves: (1) Subscription: the subscriptions set out in the subscription register are approved and the capital commitments of the limited partners are fixed in accordance with the partnership agreement. (2) Registered Office: the registered office is adopted at [street, postcode, Luxembourg], and the general partner is authorised to execute the lease and to complete the RCS notification. (3) Officers: [Name] is appointed as the EU-resident manager and authorised signatory, with sole signature authority, effective immediately. (4) Administration: opening bank accounts and all VAT, RCS and ancillary filings are authorised and confirmed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name verification and execution of the SCSp partnership agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Parties to the SCSp and, if using an online pre-check, Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) public database.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Perform a name availability search on the RCS database. Finalise the partnership agreement, subscription schedule and governance provisions. Execute the deed as a private deed, or as a notarial deed if required by the chosen asset contributions or third-party arrangements. Ensure signatures are legalised where a signatory signs outside Luxembourg and the document will be lodged in softcopy.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name and name availability check
Draft SCSp partnership agreement (contrat de société)
Subscription schedule and agreed capital commitments
Identity documents of the general partner, limited partners and manager
Power of attorney for any representative
Declarations of non-bankruptcy and fitness for the general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused or Zoned as confusingly similar, amend the name in a preferred and approved form and re-execute the partnership agreement by an amended deed before refiling.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers, RCS electronic filing portal (eDesk / guichet.lu).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the completed SCSp registration application through the LBR portal, attaching the signed partnership agreement and all required dossiers. Pay the official filing fee electronically. Address any admissibility queries raised by the RCS case officer until the registration is approved and the RCS number is allocated.
required_dossiers: Signed and legalised SCSp partnership agreement
RCS registration application form
Subscription schedule and capital proof
General partner's consent and management resolution
Registered office lease and landlord's written consent
Identity documents and criminal record extracts for managers (less than 3 months old)
Declaration of no bankruptcy / fitness
Payment receipt for the filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to an RCS query within 15 calendar days through the same eDesk file. Submit corrected resolutions, legalised signatures or an explanatory covering letter. Late responses require a new submission, but do not automatically invalidate the incorporation if cured before formal rejection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RESA publication and issuance of RCS certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) and the official electronic gazette, Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once the RCS registration is accepted, LBR publishes the required legal notice in RESA. Confirm the published entries, print the RCS extract and use the issued certificate of registration as proof of legal existence for banks, tax authorities and counterparties.
required_dossiers: RCS registration number allocated at Step 2
Approved RCS filing record
RESA publication confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RESA notice contains factual errors, file a corrective registration or rectification request with LBR within 30 days of the erroneous publication; the RCS registry will issue an amended extract.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: VAT, statistical and social security registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS) if the SCSp employs staff; STATEC for statistical declarations.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register for Luxembourg VAT with the AEDT within the statutory post-incorporation period, using the standard online registration form. Provide the ISIC 4791 activity description for online retail of 3D printers and consumables. If the SCSp hires personnel, register as an employer with the CCSS before any salary is paid. For distance sales into other EU Member States, opt into the OSS regime where advantageous.
required_dossiers: RCS extract
SCSp partnership agreement
Identity documents of partners and signatories
Description of economic activity aligned with ISIC 4791
Expected turnover and cross-border e-commerce declaration
Bank account details
CCSS employer registration form if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the VAT registration is challenged or delayed, resubmit with a precise activity narrative for online retail of hardware and consumables and provide supplementary turnover projections. Late registration interest may be waived where the first taxable transaction is not yet completed and all back filings are made promptly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business establishment authorisation and municipal/environmental filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of the Economy, General Directorate for Middle Classes; the competent municipal administration; and the Administration de l'environnement where applicable.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an application for the commercial establishment authorisation (autorisation d'établissement de commerçant) to the Ministry of the Economy, because the SCSp will operate a commercial activity from a Luxembourg establishment. If office/warehouse premises are used, complete the applicable municipal occupancy and environmental notification forms in parallel. Keep a record of the authorisation for the RCS file and for e-commerce payment providers.
required_dossiers: RCS extract and certificate of registration
SCSp partnership agreement
Identity documents and criminal record extracts of the managers
Business plan and activity description for ISIC 4791
Lease agreement and landlord's consent for the registered office and premises
Proof of professional establishment and inventory/storage details
Municipal commercial occupancy form
Environmental notification form if warehouse storage of resins is intended
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipal or ministerial authority raises objections, amend the establishment description, submit additional floor plans and lease documentation, or narrow the activity description to pure online retail warehousing without on-site manufacturing. Any refusal may be appealed under the general administrative procedure rules within 40 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy, General Directorate for Middle Classes (Ministère de l'Économie – Classes moyennes); municipal administration of the commune of the registered office; Administration de l'environnement for environmental compliance.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement de commerçant (Business Establishment Licence) and, where applicable, municipal commercial occupation permit for the warehouse/office premises. No sector-specific financial or payment licence is required for online retail of 3D printers and consumables.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Luxembourg Environment Agency), Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Biodiversity.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: No mandatory full Environmental Impact Assessment applies to online retail and low-volume warehousing of 3D printers and consumables. The activity falls within the environmental notification/registration tier of the Luxembourg 'établissements classés' scheme; a higher tier requiring a formal environmental permit applies only if resin storage quantities or hazardous waste thresholds are exceeded.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater from printing residues and resin handling must not be discharged untreated into municipal sewers; any contaminated wash-water constitutes hazardous waste. Volatile Organic Compound emissions from resin storage and printing must remain below the thresholds of EU Directive 2010/75/EU and the relevant Grand-Ducal regulations. Waste electrical and electronic equipment (3D printers) meets Luxembourg WEEE registration and take-back obligations. Resin cartridges and contaminated PPE must be disposed of under the appropriate European Waste Catalogue codes, e.g. EWC 08 03 17*.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the competent municipal fire brigade and civil defence services for any commercial premises; structural load inspection for mezzanine, racking and equipment storage; electrical installation conformity certificate; workplace risk assessment and health-and-safety clearance under the Luxembourg Law of 17 June 1994 on Occupational Health and Safety; and, where required, a positive post-visit civil defence report for the warehouse or showroom.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Luxembourg: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for income/wealth tax; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT and registration duties; primary official portal for registration and payment: myGuichet.lu (MyGuichet) and guichet.lu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign/non-resident entity making taxable B2C supplies in Luxembourg must file an online VAT registration application via MyGuichet.lu before commencing taxable activity. Required supporting documents include certificate of incorporation or equivalent, excerpt from the Luxembourg RCS or foreign trade/company register, articles/statutes, proof of business address, identity documents of partners/managers/directors, and, where no EU establishment exists, appointment of a Luxembourg fiscal representative if required by the VAT administration. Upon acceptance, AEDT issues a Luxembourg national tax number and a VAT identification number (LU followed by 8 digits), normally within 10-15 business days.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg has no IRS-style check-the-box election. An SCSp (Société en commandite spéciale) is mandatorily fiscally transparent for Luxembourg corporate income tax and net wealth tax purposes; it is not subject to Luxembourg corporate income tax in its own name. There is no statutory corporate election for transparency. Luxembourg applies ATAD-Nexus anti-hybrid and mismatch rules that may reclassify payments or deny deductions if a hybrid mismatch arises with the residence jurisdiction of a non-resident partner. Taxpayers may obtain a binding advance tax ruling from the ACD confirming the transparent classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For a taxable person established in Luxembourg, the small business VAT exemption threshold is annual taxable turnover of EUR 35,000 excluding VAT; exceeding this threshold triggers mandatory Luxembourg VAT registration. For non-established foreign sellers supplying goods or e-commerce services to Luxembourg consumers, registration is mandatory from the first taxable transaction and no general turnover threshold applies; the EU distance-sales/OVR threshold rules may in some EU-supply scenarios require use of the one-stop shop (OSS) rather than separate Luxembourg registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not currently impose a general mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control (CTC), or digital stamping requirement. Electronic invoicing is accepted where authenticity of origin, integrity of content, and readability are ensured. Luxembourg does not require acceptance of e-invoices through Peppol or a dedicated national clearance API for standard B2B sales. Businesses must retain invoice records, export-supporting documentation, and periodic VAT returns (e.g. monthly/quarterly) filed electronically via the Luxembourg eCDF / eTVA platform or through the official portal. For intra-EU supplies of goods, recapitulative statements may also be required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A 0% Luxembourg VAT rate applies to exports of goods physically dispatched or transported by the supplier or a third party to a destination outside the European Union, provided the supplier retains adequate commercial and customs proof that the goods have left the EU. For online retail of 3D printers, resin filaments, and consumables, zero-rating is available where the non-resident buyer's identity and destination address are established, transport to a non-EU country is documented, and the customs export declaration is made. Services that are directly related to exported goods or performed for non-EU customers may also qualify for zero-rating under the general B2B place-of-supply rules, subject to documentary substantiation.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (EU Single Administrative Document / export declaration) containing the MRN and customs office of export
Bill of Lading, air waybill, or courier/consignment note evidencing dispatch to the non-EU destination
Commercial invoice and packing list describing the 3D printers, resins, and consumables
Contract or purchase order of the non-EU buyer
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank/payment settlement evidence showing that export proceeds are paid from outside the EU
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT may refuse zero-rating and retroactively assess VAT at 17% plus default interest where export proof is incomplete, inconsistent, or unavailable at the time of audit. False or fraudulent export documentation may trigger administrative fines, restoration of VAT and input VAT clawback, loss of deduction rights, and, in severe intentional cases, criminal tax penalties. Luxembourg tax law requires exporters to retain all substantiating documents for at least six years. Although Luxembourg maintains no formal foreign-exchange control or statutory FX repatriation deadline for export zero-rating, the 180-day inward remittance benchmark is treated as a documentary best-practice indicator; failure to repatriate or evidence payment may heighten audit scrutiny and payment-abuse allegations.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), operating as part of the Eurosystem; prudential banking supervision is delegated to the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF); the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (CRF/Cellule de Renseignement Financier) exercises AML/CFT oversight; the Ministry of Finance retains residual sanction and monetary policy coordination powers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible; Luxembourg maintains no exchange-control legislation. Cross-border transfers on current and capital account are unrestricted under Articles 63-66 TFEU and the EU single market. The SCSp is tax-transparent, so profit remittances are made directly to partners without Luxembourg withholding tax, provided the SCSp is not characterized as an AIF (Law of 12 July 2013) and has sufficient local substance. Practical blockage points are limited to EU/UN sanctions screening, Regulation (EU) 2018/1672 cash declaration thresholds, and bank-level AML 'payment integrity' reviews; none of these impose convertibility restrictions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg imposes no timeline for repatriation, no surrender ratio, and no mandatory conversion requirement for export receipts. Revenue from online retail of 3D printers and consumables may be retained in EUR or any foreign currency in Luxembourg or foreign accounts. Only the BCL balance-of-payments statistical declaration regime applies, and penalties for non-declaration are administrative rather than currency-fiscal.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (dépôt d'attente) and Operational Settlement Account
Operational commercial account with SWIFT and e-banking
Operational account with treasury and trade finance module
Private-banking current account (generally unsuited to operating e-commerce treasury)
Wealth-management account (declined for pure operational treasury)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-High via Luxembourg-licensed e-money institutions (EMIs) such as Mangopay SA and Payconiq, and EU-passported EMIs including Wise, Airwallex, Revolut Business, Qonto and Pliant. These rails provide rapid onboarding, API-linked accounts, multi-currency IBANs and near-interbank FX. Legal and operational constraints: (i) the SCSp lacks separate legal personality, which many automated EMIs fail to underwrite - the partnership agreement, gérant/managers' mandate and RBE extract are mandatory; (ii) tax-transparent entities are frequently flagged by automated merchant acquirers; (iii) EMI client-money safeguarding is ring-fenced but not a bank deposit guarantee; (iv) most EMIs still cannot replace Tier-1 SWIFT MT103 B2B trade settlement to APAC suppliers. Recommended architecture: Stripe/Shopify payout settlement to a passported EMI sub-account for working-capital agility, with the primary clearing and liquidity account retained at BCEE or BIL.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No statutory obligation for physical presence; CSSF-compliant remote onboarding by video identification and eIDAS-qualified electronic signatures is legally acceptable. In practice, Luxembourg banks de facto require at least one authorized signatory (gérant / manager) or a local delegated director to complete an onboarding interview, normally by video call, and for non-EU entities the provision of apostilled corporate documents with certified French/German/English translations. A registered office in Luxembourg under a licensed ELF/professional services firm is mandatory for the SCSp.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp interpreted by bank underwriting as an unregulated alternative investment fund, orphan shell, or pass-through entity without commercial substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the partnership agreement (contrat de société) stating commercial object under ISIC 4791; Luxembourg RCS registration excerpt (extrait du registre de commerce); valid VAT certificate; Shopify/Stripe merchant agreements; supplier contracts for 3D printers and resin filaments; written tax-counsel confirmation that the entity is not an AIF under the Law of 12 July 2013 and is engaged in active e-commerce.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Nominal or zero seed capital profile for a limited partnership, triggering low-income / high-round-trip suspicious activity risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Capital call commitment letters executed by each partner; scheduled drawdown plan and 12-month treasury forecast; evidence of pre-funded working capital buffer; partner bank reference letters; board/manager resolution authorizing account opening and treasury mandate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-EEA beneficial-owner chain (e.g., Asia-Pacific owners of the resin/importer supply chain) raising sanctions, PEP, and source-of-wealth concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) extract; verified passports of all natural-person UBOs; source-of-wealth statement; apostilled certificates of incorporation/good standing for intermediate entities; completed sanctions, PEP and adverse-media screening consent; explanation of economic nexus to non-EU jurisdictions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-spiking card-acquirer settlement volume from Stripe and Shopify Payments, with refunds/chargebacks, creating mule-account or payment-integrity red flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Unexpired merchant-of-record agreements with Stripe (Stripe Technology Europe Ltd) and Shopify Payments; six-month historical settlement statements from prior operations (if available); chargeback ratio report (target <0.5%); PCI DSS attestation of compliance (AoC); policy to separate settlement accounts from disbursement accounts and to avoid same-day pass-through transfers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-transparent SCSp classification misunderstood by underwriters as a withholding-risk structure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Tax-counsel opinion confirming SCSp pass-through treatment, absence of Luxembourg corporate income tax at entity level, and no withholding on distributions to partners; CRS/FATCA self-certification forms; extract from the domestic law codified provisions on SCSp; lodging authority letters where applicable.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections are routed via SWIFT MT103 from the partner's bank to the SCSp's Luxembourg EUR account, with remittance narrative stating 'Capital contribution - participation in SCSp - direct investment (ISIC 4791 operating entity)' and the BCL balance-of-payments statistical purpose code for direct investment equity/other capital. The bank verifies source of funds via the capital call notice, updated partners register, RBE extract and partner bank reference; funds may initially be parked in a capital call/dépôt d'attente account and drawn down against signed drawdown certificates. For non-EU partners, the sending bank's FATF status materially affects payment integrity review, and any cash transfer above the Regulation (EU) 2018/1672 threshold must be declared at the external border; sanctions-profiling unmatched narratives will cause rejection.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: SEPA and TARGET2 instant transfers for EU suppliers of packaging and spare parts; SWIFT MT103 for non-EU supplier settlements (USD, CNH, or CNY) on 30-60 day open account terms; commercial letters of credit under UCP 600 (MT700) issued via BIL or BGL BNP Paribas for large resin and filament bulk purchases from China; documentary collections (CAD / D/P) for repeat medium-value orders; chargeback funding to card acquirers via standard settlement return mechanics. Treasury reconciliation is performed daily using Stripe/Shopify settlement files mapped to bank statements; all derivative, LC and clearing mandates are executed by the gérant (manager) for and on behalf of the SCSp, which, although lacking separate legal personality under Luxembourg law, holds a patrimoine commun and may be party to contracts in its own commercial name; banks may additionally require a GP covenant or LP comfort letter for ISDA/CSA thresholds.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright EUR/USD and EUR/CNH deliverable forwards for import payable hedging
EUR/CNY non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) where mainland China invoice exposure cannot be settled deliverable
FX swaps (swap contre dépôt) for short-term cross-currency liquidity pre-funding
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD and EUR/CNH) under ISDA/CSA for material recurring trade flows
Plain-vanilla FX options (EUR call / USD put and EUR call / CNH put) for tail-risk protection, subject to EMIR reporting and PRIIPs/KID assessment if offered by EU counterparties
Interest-rate products are excluded from the initial mandate unless debt financing is introduced, at which point a refreshed derivatives governance policy is required

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts publication (balance sheet, profit and loss account and notes) — mandatory only where the Luxembourg SCSp is a large or medium undertaking; otherwise exempt from RCS filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the financial year-end; for a 31 December year-end: no later than 30 June (or 31 July where shareholder approval is dated 30 June)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing produces an RCS reminder and administrative fine for the general partner or appointed manager of up to EUR 1,500; persistent non-compliance after formal notice may lead to a court-ordered strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual municipal business tax return (impôt commercial communal) — compulsory for the SCSp if it carries on a commercial undertaking through a Luxembourg permanent establishment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The ACD-issued standard deadline for the preceding tax year is normally 31 December of the following calendar year; extensions may be granted in the annual tax filing schedule
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing triggers unilateral assessment by ACD, late-filing fine of up to EUR 1,000, monthly late-payment interest on the assessed municipal business tax, and potential enforcement against the partnership's assets.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership (RBE) declaration update — triggered by every transfer or acquisition of a limited-partner interest
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 calendar days of any transfer or change in beneficial ownership; if no change occurs, the general partner must document an annual RBE consistency confirmation at the calendar year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to update the RBE may attract administrative fines up to EUR 250,000; intentional misstatements may result in criminal fines and imprisonment, in addition to suspension of access to RCS services.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory accounting records and source evidence made available for Luxembourg tax review — annual closure of accounts for the transparent partnership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) upon request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Prepared no later than the municipal business tax filing deadline; retained for ten years after closure of the financial year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Inadequate records allow ACD to estimate the partnership income and assess taxes and late-payment interest; accounting law penalties and partner-level income tax reassessments may follow.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory audit by a Luxembourg cabinet de révision agréé is required only if the SCSp exceeds at least two of three thresholds: balance-sheet total above EUR 4.4 million; net turnover above EUR 8.8 million; average workforce above 50 employees. An e-commerce SCSp below these thresholds is exempt, unless a partner representing 10% of capital requests an audit or the tax administration orders one.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Lux GAAP) under the law of 19 December 2002 on annual accounts, as amended by the law of 10 December 2018 implementing EU Directive 2013/34/EU; IFRS as adopted in the EU may be used voluntarily for consolidated or group accounts of eligible undertakings.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Luxembourg law does not impose a separate annual UBO return for an SCSp. However, on every transfer of a partnership interest the general partner must file an RBE update within 30 days. At the annual closing, the general partner must reconcile the internal register of partners with the RBE database and document that the beneficial-owner information remains accurate, including after silent assignments or changes in indirect control.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (register of limited partners' interests and transfers)
Register of Directors (register of general partners and management powers)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,300–2,700 per annum (EUR 1,200–2,500) for a Luxembourg domiciliation/registered-office agent and corporate secretarial service
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 14,000–27,000 (EUR 12,000–25,000) if audit becomes compulsory; not required for a micro or small SCSp e-commerce operation

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% aggregate CIT + solidarity surcharge + Luxembourg City municipal business tax (15% corporate income tax + 7% solidarity surcharge + 6.75% municipal business tax)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SCSp is fiscally transparent; no CIT or municipal business tax at partnership level. Luxembourg-resident corporate partners are taxed on their profit share at the standard 24.94% Luxembourg City rate, subject to participation exemption, IP box relief, and other treaty/ATAD mechanisms. Non-resident partners are generally exempt from Luxembourg tax unless the SCSp operates a Luxembourg permanent establishment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 720 — Annual Luxembourg Corporate Income Tax Return (Déclaration pour l’impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) filed via MyGuichet.lu e-Filing portal of the Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD). For a transparent SCSp, the corporate partner's CIT return is used to report its allocable share of SCSp profit; the SCSp itself does not file Form 720 as a taxable entity.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return; quarterly CIT prepayments are due 10 March, 10 June, 10 September, 10 December.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing due within 5 months after the financial year-end. For calendar-year entities, the deadline is 31 May. An extension to 31 December is available through MyGuichet.lu if a pro forma request is made on or before the original deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Entity identification data: corporate partner name, RCS number, fiscal number, address, financial year-end, ISIC 4791 / NAICS 443142 business description.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the partner is a non-resident without a Luxembourg permanent establishment, no Form 720 is filed. If a Luxembourg PE exists, identify the PE, its Luxembourg fiscal number, and the head office details.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting pre-tax profit derived from unconsolidated financial statements, adjusted for tax deductible expenses, non-deductible items, and exempt income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only profits attributable to the Luxembourg PE are reportable. Apply the OECD profit attribution principles and Luxembourg Article 155bis LIR rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of taxable income after loss carry-forwards, participation exemptions, and tax credits. Includes the schedule of losses used.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loss carry-forward may not exceed the PE's Luxembourg tax results; cross-border loss relief between PE and foreign head office is not available.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: CIT at 15%, solidarity surcharge at 7% of CIT, municipal business tax rate according to the commune (Luxembourg City 6.75%), advance payments, and final balance due.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute CIT and solidarity surcharge on the PE taxable base; municipal business tax applies to the PE if it forms a fixed establishment within the commune.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a 0.6% monthly late-payment interest on unpaid CIT, capped at 10%. Deliberate non-filing can lead to ex officio assessment, a surcharge up to 10% of the tax due, and criminal prosecution for tax fraud.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% statutory withholding on distributions treated as dividends from a Luxembourg resident company. An SCSp is fiscally transparent; distributions to partners are not dividends and are not subject to Luxembourg WHT unless the partner is deemed to have a Luxembourg PE and the distribution is recharacterized as a taxable dividend.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: For treaty relief on actual Luxembourg dividend payments, the recipient must submit a written relief request to the Luxembourg tax office (ACD) using the administrative form for reduced withholding, attach a valid tax residence certificate (TRC) from the taxpayer's residence state, and provide evidence of beneficial ownership. For SCSp profit distributions, no dividend WHT or DTA relief is required, but non-resident partners may need to file a Luxembourg tax return if the SCSp has a Luxembourg PE or Luxembourg-source business income.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg generally imposes no statutory withholding on interest and royalties paid to non-residents, except profit-sharing loans recharacterized as constructive dividends. Under the EU Interest & Royalties Directive, associated EU companies may access a 0% rate. Outbound royalties to treaty countries commonly attract 0% withholding if the recipient is the beneficial owner.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Compulsory Local File for controlled cross-border transactions exceeding EUR 500,000; Master File if the multinational group has consolidated turnover of at least EUR 50 million; Country-by-Country Report if group consolidated revenue is at least EUR 750 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not maintain a separate Economic Substance Regulations statute like the UAE. Instead, substance requirements are enforced through the participation exemption, permanent establishment attribution, ATAD CFC rules, and the general anti-abuse doctrine (abus de droit / Statutory Anti-Avoidance rule under AO 6 and Luxembourg case law). To avoid treaty-shopping or PE recharacterization, the SCSp must maintain a genuine Luxembourg office, local bank account, local management decisions, employees, and business records for the online retail of 3D printers and resin filaments.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly filing false Form 720, understating SCSp profit, concealing e-commerce sales, or directing customer payments to offshore accounts while booking minimal Luxembourg revenue.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment for up to 10 years, late interest of 0.6% per month, financial penalty up to EUR 250,000, and imprisonment of the responsible individuals under Luxembourg criminal tax law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the general partner may have the corporate veil pierced; they are jointly liable for unpaid taxes, face travel bans and asset seizures, and may be sentenced to imprisonment for fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: SCSp has no real Luxembourg premises, no resident director, no substance, and uses a shell structure to claim treaty benefits or avoid tax on online retail margins.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ACD may disregard the SCSp, recharacterize it as taxable or opaque, deny treaty benefits, impose 24.94% CIT on deemed underlying profits, and apply 15% WHT on deemed distributions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The nominal corporate general partner and its directors are personally exposed to restitution claims, disqualification, and criminal sanctions for facilitating abusive structures.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Cross-border intercompany purchase or resale of 3D printers and consumables at non-arm's-length margins, without preparing Local File when related-party transactions exceed EUR 500,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: A transfer pricing adjustment, secondary adjustment recharacterizing excess profit as dividends, refusal of deduction, penalties up to 10% of the adjusted profit, and monthly interest accrual.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly execute unfavorable pricing without supporting documentation can be held jointly liable for the adjusted tax, interest, and penalties, and may face criminal prosecution for evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: SCSp accepting anonymous crypto payments or cash for high-value 3D printers, failing to identify ultimate beneficial owners, or transacting with sanctioned parties while processing through Stripe or Shopify Payments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to EUR 5 million and imprisonment up to 5 years under Luxembourg law of 12 November 2004, as amended; administrative fines up to EUR 1 million; freezing orders and forfeiture of assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the SCSp's authorized agent are criminally liable, subject to civil restitution, disqualification from conducting financial services, travel bans, and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Structuring SCSp profit distributions as 'royalties' or 'interest' from the Luxembourg entity to a related party without legal substance, to avoid the 15% dividend withholding tax or the transparent pass-through regime.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reclassification as constructive dividends subject to 15% WHT if the recipient is a shareholder, plus late-interest, penalties, and potential deemed income assessments.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Designing and approving sham payment structures exposes directors to personal liability for the grossed-up withholding tax, damages for breach of fiduciary duty, and criminal sanction in fraudulent cases.
